title: Card that responds to its container
summary: @container: the same card stacks in a narrow slot and goes sideways in a wide one.
explanation: A media query asks how wide the window is. A container query asks how wide the card's own slot is. container-type: inline-size on .slot makes it a query container, and @container (min-width: 300px) then applies only to elements inside the slot that is at least that wide.

Both slots hold the identical card. The narrow slot (one share of the page) keeps it stacked; the wide slot (two shares) switches it to a thumbnail beside the text. That is how a component can work in a sidebar and in a main column without knowing where it is.
The query styles the container's descendants, never the container itself, which is why the card sits inside the slot instead of being the slot.
tryThis: Change 300px to 500px: the wide slot drops back to the stacked card.
Change grid-template-columns on .page to 1fr 1fr: both slots become equally wide, so both cards make the same choice.
Remove container-type: inline-size from .slot: the @container rule stops applying anywhere.

children.text: The same card, thumbnail beside the text.
